question.text: Fund PPI (Cat III Pre-IPO strategy) bought 2,50,000 shares of Company ABC from the promoter on 15-Jan-2023 at INR 120/share via private placement. The subsequent IPO issue price (15-Jun-2023) was INR 130/share. What is the Pre-IPO DISCOUNT captured by the fund?

explanation.text: The Logic: Discount per share = 130 - 120 = INR 10. As % of Issue Price = 10/130 = 7.69% (PDF Example 10.8 rounds to 7.70%). The PDF cites this as the Pre-IPO discount basis. The Trap: Option B uses invested price as denominator (8.33%) — wrong convention. Option C is absurd. Option D uses the wrong share count. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) touches Pre-IPO marketing; XIX-E manager-side calc tests the discount formula. Manager's Pro-Tip: Pre-IPO positions are locked-in per SEBI (ICDR) Regulations post listing; for NAV purposes the fund values these at IPO issue price during the lock-in, with an illiquidity discount — typically 10-15% — reversed gradually as lock-in unwinds.
